newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar but closed almost unchanged against the basket of foreign currencies on Tuesday after the dollar's rise in Europe, dealers said.
"The local market was very quiet. The shekel weakened against the dollar following the rise of the U.S. currency in Europe," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
"The Bank of Israel had to intervene several times in trading, buying dollars to keep the basket at seven percent below the slope," he added.

The shekel is allowed to trade in a band of seven percent above or below a sloping midpoint designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.1970 against 3.1920 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5648 shekels against 3.5644 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8467 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8593 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0772 shekels per mark against 2.0855 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1970 shekels.
